amendment_history.note: الإصدار الأصلي -- تصديقاً على نظام البريد بموجب قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (149) وتاريخ 06/03/1443هـ، ونشر في جريدة أم القرى بتاريخ 16/03/1443هـ. يحل هذا النظام محل نظام البريد الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي رقم (م/4) وتاريخ 21/2/1406هـ (مؤكد من مصادر ثانوية متعددة؛ رقم المادة الحاملة لنص الإلغاء تحديداً غير مؤكد هذه الجولة -- انظر postal_repeal_clause_article_number_unconfirmed). هذا المسار يثبت نص 20 مادة فقط (من أصل 37 مادة يُرجَّح أنها العدد الإجمالي الصحيح) -- انظر postal_articles_21_37_not_ingested وpostal_art_count_37_vs_38.

نقل إداري/إحلال مصطلحات (غير مثبت كتعديل نصي على مادة بعينها هذه الجولة): إحلال عبارة 'تنظيم الهيئة العامة للنقل' محل عبارة 'تنظيم هيئة الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات'، وعبارة 'وزارة النقل والخدمات اللوجستية' محل عبارة 'وزارة الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات'، أينما وردتا في نظام البريد والأوامر والقرارات والوثائق ذات الصلة بقطاع البريد -- منقول عبر تجميع بحث ويب (WebSearch)، لم يُقرأ نصه الأصلي مباشرة هذه الجولة (laws.boe.gov.sa وtga.gov.sa كانا غير متاحين). مؤكد ظرفياً عبر استضافة الهيئة العامة للنقل للائحة التنفيذية لنظام البريد على موقعها، وعبر قرارها الإداري رقم (١/٧/٢٠٢٣/٣) الموافق على جدول مخالفات وعقوبات نظام البريد. انظر postal_com705_transfer_not_primary_fetched.

chapter_structure.title_ar: تخليص المواد البريدية (جزئي -- المادة 20 فقط من أصل 20-22؛ انظر postal_chapter5_partial_coverage)

verification_methodology_note:
PRIMARY SOURCE ACCESS: laws.boe.gov.sa's live portal returned HTTP 503 on every attempt this pass (multiple retries, both via the WebFetch tool and via direct curl -- curl failed at the TLS-handshake stage, exit code 35, suggesting the destination itself is unreachable from this session's egress path rather than a simple rate-limit). archive.org/wayback/available confirmed a snapshot exists (20260228191414), but the web.archive.org domain itself is categorically blocked for this session's WebFetch tool ("Claude Code is unable to fetch from web.archive.org" -- tested against an unrelated, known-good URL to confirm this is a blanket domain block, not a one-off failure). www.tga.gov.sa (General Authority for Transport) and site.eastlaws.com likewise failed to connect at the TLS layer via curl (exit 35) and returned 503 via WebFetch. mot.gov.sa (Ministry of Transport and Logistics Services) returned 302/404 with no substantive content. www.uqn.gov.sa (Umm Al-Qura Official Gazette, the law's actual publication venue) is reachable but is a pure client-side-rendered single-page application: curl (with a real browser User-Agent, and again with a Googlebot User-Agent) retrieved only the ~1-2KB navigation shell, never the article body, for both the law's own gazette page and its Executive Regulation's gazette page. qanoonsa.com and qanoniah.com are likewise client-side-rendered; their site search successfully located this law's page and closely-related administrative decisions (see below) by title, but article body text was not present in the server-delivered HTML. SECONDARY SOURCES THAT DID YIELD CONTENT: (1) nezams.com's page (https://nezams.com/نظام-البريد-2/, fetched live via curl with a realistic browser User-Agent -- nezams.com returns HTTP 406 to a bare curl User-Agent, but 200 with browser-like headers) is server-side-rendered and embeds all 38 of its own listed article
  • elements' full text directly in the HTML (no JavaScript execution needed). Its own page metadata (an og:description meta tag and an on-page details table, both read directly from the raw HTML) states: Royal Decree (م/22) 08/03/1443H; Council of Ministers Resolution (149) 06/03/1443H; publication date 16/03/1443H; status "ساري" (in force); "التعديلات: لم يجرى عليه تعديل" (no amendment has been made to it) -- this last field is nezams's own amendment-tracking field for the LAW itself, and it reads "no amendment," consistent with this build's treatment of the CoM 705 regulatory transfer as an administrative reassignment rather than a tracked textual amendment. (2) A WebFetch of lexismiddleeast.com's page for Council of Ministers Resolution 149 (CabinetDecision_149_1443) independently corroborated: Royal Decree M/22 08/03/1443H; CoM Resolution 149 06/03/1443H; the predecessor law (Royal Decree M/4, 21/2/1406H, explicitly named as replaced); and, critically, an independently-scraped chapter/فصل breakdown with article ranges: الفصل الأول (عام) 1-3، الفصل الثاني (تراخيص) 4-10، الفصل الثالث (منافسة) 11، الفصل الرابع (التزامات وحقوق) 12-19، الفصل الخامس (تخليص) 20-22، الفصل السادس (مسؤولية وسرية) 23-26، الفصل السابع (رقابة وتفتيش) 27-29، الفصل الثامن (مخالفات وعقوبات) 30-33، الفصل التاسع (ختامية) 34-37 -- totalling 37 articles. (3) Arab News (an independent English-language press outlet, fetched live this pass) quotes Saudi Communications Minister Abdullah Al-Swaha directly and by name stating the new law "includes 37 articles" -- this is a strong, named-official-source corroboration of the 37-article total, independent of lexismiddleeast's own structural scrape. CRITICAL FINDING -- nezams.com's OWN CONTENT IS CORRUPTED FROM ARTICLE 21 ONWARD: nezams.com's page lists 38 numbered
  • elements (N=1..38) with correctly-labelled Arabic ordinal headings (المادة الأولى ... الثامنة والثلاثون) and, for articles 1-20, correctly-topical فصل headings that EXACTLY match lexismiddleeast's independent chapter/range breakdown at every chapter boundary through article 20 (فصل أول at art.1, فصل ثاني at art.4, فصل ثالث at art.11, فصل رابع at art.12, فصل خامس at art.20). However, starting at article 21, the BODY TEXT under each heading is verbatim content from an entirely DIFFERENT, unrelated law -- Saudi Arabia's Solid Municipal Waste Management Law (نظام إدارة النفايات البلدية الصلبة, Royal Decree M/48, 17/9/1434H): article 21's body discusses "إدارة النفايات" (waste management) and reporting incidents to "المركز" (a Center, not الهيئة/التنظيم as used throughout articles 1-20); article 25 discusses financial guarantees for waste-management facility operators; articles 26-35 discuss waste producer/carrier civil and penal liability, a criminal penalty of up to 30 million SAR for illegal waste dumping, and a violations committee -- none of this is postal-sector content. Article 37's body text is literally the operative repeal clause of the SOLID WASTE law ("يحل هذا النظام محل نظام إدارة النفايات البلدية الصلبة، الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي رقم (م/48) وتاريخ 17/9/1434هـ"), not the Postal Law's own repeal clause. This corruption was independently re-confirmed via a second, separate curl fetch of the identical URL (byte-identical HTML both times, confirming this is a stable, reproducible defect on nezams.com's own page for this law -- not a transient proxy/caching artifact of this session). Consequence: nezams.com is treated as RELIABLE for articles 1-20 (topically and structurally cross-validated against lexismiddleeast's independent scrape at every chapter boundary) and UNRELIABLE/UNUSABLE for articles 21 onward, including for confirming the true total article count (its own "1..38" sidebar listing cannot be trusted once its underlying content is known to be corrupted from article 21). The 37-article total from lexismiddleeast + Arab News/the Minister's own statement is treated as the best-supported figure; nezams's "38" is documented as unresolved, not adopted. WHAT THIS BUILD INGESTS: only Articles 1-20 (of a reported 37-article law) are ingested as verified article records this pass -- the first five فصول through the start of الفصل الخامس (تخليص المواد البريدية), for which only Article 20 itself (of that chapter's three articles, 20-22) was retrievable with reliable, uncorrupted text. Articles 21-37 (18 articles: the remainder of الفصل الخامس, plus فصول السادس through التاسع -- liability/confidentiality, supervision/inspection, violations/penalties, and final provisions including the predecessor-repeal and enactment-date clauses) are NOT ingested this pass: no source reachable this pass could supply their verbatim text with confidence. This is a deliberate, disclosed partial-coverage build, consistent with this corpus's binding instruction that an honest "could not confirm" is preferable to fabricating or paraphrasing plausible-sounding article text. See known_unresolved_discrepancies for the specific gaps, the sources attempted, and leads for a follow-up pass (a small number of un-sourced fragments surfaced via web-search AI synthesis -- e.g. a liability clause resembling Article 23, penalty amounts resembling Article 31, and a 180-day enactment clause -- are recorded there as LEADS ONLY, explicitly not ingested as verified article text, since no specific fetched/checkable document could be pointed to for them). REGULATORY-TRANSFER FINDING (CoM Resolution 705, 27/12/1443H): a WebSearch AI synthesis (not a direct primary-source fetch, since laws.boe.gov.sa/tga.gov.sa were both unreachable this pass) reports that CoM Resolution 705 substitutes "تنظيم الهيئة العامة للنقل" for "تنظيم هيئة الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات" and "وزارة النقل والخدمات اللوجستية" for "وزارة الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات" wherever they appear in the Postal Law and related orders/decisions/documents relevant to the postal sector. This is corroborated circumstantially by two independently-fetched facts: (a) www.tga.gov.sa's own Regulations portal lists "اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام البريد" (this Law's own Executive Regulation) at tga.gov.sa/Regulations/Regulation/4017 -- i.e. TGA now hosts/administers the Postal Law's implementing regulation; (b) qanoonsa.com's site search independently surfaced a 2023 TGA-issued administrative decision, "الهيئة العامة للنقل: قرار رقم (١/٧/٢٠٢٣/٣) الموافقة على جدول مخالفات وعقوبات نظام البريد" (TGA's own approval of the Postal Law's violations/penalties schedule), matching the same instrument independently referenced by lexismiddleeast.com as "AdministrativeDecision_1_7_2023_3_1444." Both are consistent with TGA (not CITC) now administering postal-sector secondary instruments, in the manner CoM 705 is reported to direct. However, CoM 705's own primary text was not directly fetched/read this pass (both laws.boe.gov.sa and tga.gov.sa were unreachable), so this finding rests on secondary/circumstantial corroboration, not a first-hand primary-source read -- flagged accordingly. Critically, nezams.com's own Article 1 definitions (اs originally enacted, ingested in this build as postal_art_001) still read التنظيم/الوزارة/الوزير/الهيئة as تنظيم/وزارة/وزير/هيئة الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات -- i.e. the ORIGINAL, pre-705 terminology -- and this build does NOT know, and did not attempt to guess, whether BOE's own current/consolidated display of this article has since been updated to reflect CoM 705's substitution. This is recorded as an open discrepancy, not resolved by assumption in either direction. No legal text is altered beyond whitespace/line-break normalization needed to render nezams.com's HTML as plain text (converting literal
    tags to newlines; collapsing runs of spaces/tabs/non-breaking-space/zero-width characters to a single space per line; stripping the leading الفصل/title/bare-ordinal heading lines that nezams.com repeats at the top of the first article of each فصل, relocating that information into chapter_structure/section_ar instead). Arabic governs; no translation/paraphrase/interpretation performed on the Arabic article text (English descriptions in this note and in document_en/issuing_authority_en are for indexing only). Read-only over input; deterministic over outputs.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: Articles 21 through 37 (the remainder of الفصل الخامس/تخليص المواد البريدية [arts. 21-22], plus الفصل السادس/المسؤولية والسرية [23-26], الفصل السابع/الرقابة والتفتيش [27-29], الفصل الثامن/المخالفات والعقوبات [30-33], and الفصل التاسع/أحكام ختامية [34-37]) are NOT ingested in this build. No source reachable this pass (laws.boe.gov.sa live or Wayback, tga.gov.sa, mot.gov.sa, uqn.gov.sa gazette, qanoonsa.com, qanoniah.com, site.eastlaws.com) could supply their verbatim text with confidence -- see verification_methodology_note for the specific failure mode for each. A small number of un-sourced fragments surfaced via WebSearch AI synthesis (not a direct, checkable document fetch) are recorded here as LEADS ONLY for a follow-up pass, explicitly NOT ingested: a fragment resembling an Article 23 liability clause ('مقدم الخدمة مسؤول عن التأخر، أو الخطأ في تسليم أي مادة بريدية، أو فقدها، أو تلفها...'); a fragment resembling an Article 31 penalty clause (fine up to 5,000,000 SAR plus licence suspension/cancellation); and a fragment resembling a final enactment clause ('نظام البريد ينشر في الجريدة الرسمية، ويكون نافذاً بعد مائة وثمانين يوماً من تاريخ نشره' -- 180 days after gazette publication). None of these carry a specific, re-fetchable source document this pass could point to, so none are ingested as verified article text.

nezams.com's own page for this law (https://nezams.com/نظام-البريد-2/) lists 38 numbered article <li> elements with correctly-topical فصل headings matching lexismiddleeast.com's independent structural breakdown through article 20, but the BODY TEXT under every heading from article 21 onward is verbatim content from an entirely different, unrelated law: Saudi Arabia's Solid Municipal Waste Management Law (نظام إدارة النفايات البلدية الصلبة, Royal Decree M/48, 17/9/1434H) -- e.g. article 21 discusses waste-management incident reporting to 'المركز'; article 29 sets a criminal penalty of up to 30,000,000 SAR for illegal waste dumping; article 37's body is literally that OTHER law's own repeal clause naming Royal Decree M/48. This was independently re-confirmed via a second, separate curl fetch of the identical URL hours apart (byte-identical HTML both times), confirming a stable, reproducible defect on nezams.com's own page for this law, not a transient fetch artifact. Consequence: nezams.com is treated as reliable for Articles 1-20 only (independently structurally cross-validated against lexismiddleeast.com at every chapter boundary) and unusable for articles 21 onward or for confirming the true total article count.

Two independent sources agree on 37 total articles: (a) lexismiddleeast.com's own structural scrape of Council of Ministers Resolution 149's page, giving nine فصول with article ranges summing to exactly 37; (b) Arab News, quoting Saudi Communications Minister Abdullah Al-Swaha directly and by name, that the new law 'includes 37 articles.' nezams.com's own page lists a sidebar/navigation range of '1' through '38', which would suggest 38 -- but given nezams.com's own body-text content is confirmed corrupted (mixed with an unrelated law) from article 21 onward (see postal_nezams_corruption_articles_21_38), this '38' figure is NOT treated as reliable. This build treats 37 as the best-supported total article count for the Postal Law, but this was not independently confirmed by directly reading the primary BOE source's own article listing this pass (BOE was unreachable). article_count in this file (20) reflects only the articles actually ingested, not the law's true total; see official_reported_article_count.

This Law's replacement of the predecessor 1406H Postal Law (Royal Decree M/4, 21/2/1406H) is corroborated by multiple independent sources: the enacting Council of Ministers Resolution 149's own recitals (ingested verbatim in preamble_ar: 'وبعد الاطلاع على نظام البريد، الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي رقم (م/4) وتاريخ 21/2/1406هـ'); lexismiddleeast.com's structural summary explicitly stating the new law 'replaces the previous postal law issued by Royal Decree No. (م/4), dated 21/02/1406H'; and a search-engine-indexed excerpt attributed to the BOE law-detail page itself reading verbatim 'هذا النظام يحل محل نظام البريد الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي (م/4) بتاريخ 1406/2/21هـ.' BOE also separately catalogues the predecessor as its own distinct law page (نظام البريد 1406هـ, BOE lawId 87aa6473-8e77-4dc5-b45d-a9a700f2e50f -- its URL/title confirmed via search, page itself not fetched this pass since laws.boe.gov.sa was unreachable). However, the OPERATIVE repeal clause is expected to sit in الفصل التاسع (أحكام ختامية, arts. 34-37), which is NOT among the 20 articles ingested this pass -- so the exact article number carrying this clause is NOT independently confirmed by this build; only the fact and target (M/4, 1406H) of the replacement are confirmed, via recitals and secondary sources, not via this Law's own operative closing articles.

Council of Ministers Resolution 705, 27/12/1443H, is reported (via WebSearch AI synthesis, not a direct primary-source fetch -- laws.boe.gov.sa and tga.gov.sa were both unreachable this pass) to substitute 'تنظيم الهيئة العامة للنقل' for 'تنظيم هيئة الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات,' and 'وزارة النقل والخدمات اللوجستية' for 'وزارة الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات,' wherever they appear in the Postal Law and related orders/decisions/documents concerning the postal sector -- transferring regulatory oversight of the postal sector from the communications sector (CITC/Ministry of Communications and IT) to the General Authority for Transport (TGA) and the Ministry of Transport and Logistics Services. This is corroborated circumstantially by two independently-fetched facts: (a) www.tga.gov.sa's own Regulations portal lists this Law's own Executive Regulation (اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام البريد, tga.gov.sa/Regulations/Regulation/4017); (b) qanoonsa.com's site search independently surfaced a 2023 TGA-issued administrative decision approving the Postal Law's violations/penalties schedule ('الهيئة العامة للنقل: قرار رقم (١/٧/٢٠٢٣/٣) الموافقة على جدول مخالفات وعقوبات نظام البريد'), matching the same instrument independently referenced by lexismiddleeast.com as AdministrativeDecision_1_7_2023_3_1444. Both are consistent with TGA (not CITC) now administering postal-sector secondary instruments. This build treats the CoM 705 transfer as a confirmed, real administrative reassignment (multiple independent corroborating facts) but explicitly NOT as a confirmed textual amendment of any specific numbered article of the Postal Law itself -- no source reachable this pass showed CoM 705's own primary text or identified which, if any, specific articles it edits; nezams.com's own amendment-tracking field for this Law separately reads 'لم يجرى عليه تعديل' (no amendment made), consistent with treating this as an administrative/terminology matter rather than a tracked textual amendment.

Article 1 (postal_art_001), as ingested from nezams.com, defines التنظيم/الوزارة/الوزير/الهيئة as تنظيم/وزارة/وزير/هيئة الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات -- i.e. the ORIGINAL 2021/1443H-enactment terminology, predating CoM Resolution 705's later (27/12/1443H) reported substitution of the General Authority for Transport/Ministry of Transport and Logistics Services in its place (see postal_com705_transfer_not_primary_fetched). This build does not know -- and did not attempt to guess -- whether BOE's own current/consolidated display of Article 1 has since been updated to reflect that substitution, since laws.boe.gov.sa was unreachable this pass. The text ingested here is transcribed verbatim from nezams.com exactly as that source presents it, without correction in either direction; this is flagged as an open discrepancy pending direct BOE access in a follow-up pass.

الفصل الخامس (تخليص المواد البريدية) spans Articles 20-22 per lexismiddleeast.com's independent structural breakdown, but only Article 20 itself is ingested in this build (Articles 21-22 fall within the range whose text could not be reliably retrieved this pass -- see postal_articles_21_37_not_ingested). chapter_structure in this file records الفصل الخامس's ingested range as '20' only, not the chapter's true '20-22' range, to avoid implying coverage this build does not have.

BOE separately catalogues the predecessor 1406H Postal Law as its own distinct law page (نظام البريد 1406هـ, Royal Decree م/4, 21/2/1406هـ; BOE lawId 87aa6473-8e77-4dc5-b45d-a9a700f2e50f). This page's existence, title, and URL were confirmed via search-engine results this pass, but the page itself (e.g. to directly confirm its status field now reads لاغي/repealed) was not fetched, since laws.boe.gov.sa was unreachable this pass. This is documented as confirmed historical/background context only, not ingested as articles, consistent with this corpus's practice for confirmed predecessor supersessions.
